events.body:
## Outcome

Users can follow reputable maintainers, reviewers, security researchers, mirror operators, organizations, and moderation groups without accepting one global trust authority.

## Scope

- Represent signed scoped lists with provenance, delegation, composition, expiration, revocation, and version history.
- Allow local override, multiple simultaneous lists, conflict visibility, appeals, and privacy-preserving follows.
- Separate trust by role and repository/community scope so reputation is never universal by default.

## Acceptance criteria

- Lists merge and verify across clients while preserving issuer, scope, and revocation.
- Compromised or malicious list drills support fast revocation and visible local recovery.
- No essential repository access, identity, or contribution path requires following a list.
- Linked automated evidence covers supported platforms, failure paths, rollback/recovery, documentation, and telemetry before closure.

## Delivery and dependencies

- Portfolio tier: **P1 community trust**
- Milestone: **Collaboration public beta**
- Numeric priority: **41 of 44** (1 is highest)
- Depends on: #484, #485
- Assignee: unassigned until an accountable owner accepts the epic; fund independently releasable child issues rather than this umbrella epic.

## Progress baseline

**10% as of 2026-07-22.** Signed identity/profile and federation primitives exist; scoped list schemas, composition, override, appeals, and cross-client workflows remain. Progress may not exceed 85% without end-to-end validation or 95% without security, documentation, telemetry, and rollout evidence.

## Verification and measures

Primary measures: Active lists, cross-client verification, revocation time, overrides, appeals, and abuse reports. Closure requires linked test runs, operational evidence, and current user-facing documentation.
events.title: Create scoped community-operated trust lists
